overview: Portugal is the westernmost country of mainland Europe, on the Iberian Peninsula. Its capital and largest city is Lisbon. In the 1400s and 1500s Portuguese sailors led Europe's voyages of exploration, and Portugal built an empire across Africa, Asia and South America; Portuguese is now spoken by more than 250 million people, most of them in Brazil. Portugal joined what is now the European Union in 1986.

geography.text: Mainland Portugal faces the Atlantic along a long coastline of beaches and cliffs. The north is hilly and green, while the south, especially the Algarve, is drier and sunnier. The Tagus and the Douro rivers flow west across the country from Spain to the sea. Portugal also includes two groups of Atlantic islands, the Azores and Madeira.

history.text: Portugal became an independent kingdom in the 1100s, with borders that have barely changed since. In the 1400s and 1500s its sailors explored the coasts of Africa, reached India and Brazil, and built a trading empire across the globe. A revolution in 1910 ended the monarchy, and the peaceful Carnation Revolution of 1974 ended decades of dictatorship.

events.title: Kingdom recognised
events.text: Portugal is recognised as an independent kingdom.

events.title: Sea route to India
events.text: Vasco da Gama reaches India by sailing around Africa.

events.title: Brazil reached
events.text: Pedro Álvares Cabral lands in Brazil.

events.title: Lisbon earthquake
events.text: An earthquake and tsunami destroy much of Lisbon.

events.title: Carnation Revolution
events.text: A largely peaceful military coup ends dictatorship and leads to democracy.
